newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London sink after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London sink after U.S. data.

text.p: Hong stocks traded in London took a beating from stronger than expected U.S. housing starts on Tuesday, which sent U.S. Treasury bonds lower, but gleaned some support from strong sterling, dealers said.

By 1454 GMT the Hang Seng London Reference Index was off 121.70 points at 12,693.67. One dealer said if T-bonds continued to drop and Wall Street closed around 20 to 30 points down, the Hang Seng index in Hong Kong could open some 100 points lower.
"The strong housing starts data took the bond market by surprise and there was quite a sharp sell-off in Hong Kong stocks immediately after that," he said.
"The market would be even weaker but sterling is very strong which is helping HSBC," he added.
Shares in HSBC Holdings were down at HK$154.60 in London, compared with a close of 155.00 in Hong Kong.
U.S. housing starts rose 9.2 percent in November, the largest rise since July 1995.
